message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_22b3b83e1afe", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 219, "mechanism": "The write-path condition `full_cur || full_wr || drop_frame_reg` can be evaluated true when s_axis_tvalid is low (idle bus). If that happens, the next-state logic may set `drop_frame_next=1` without a real beat, which later forces `wr_ptr_cur` to stall on the true last beat and triggers an extra accepted frame that appears on m_axis_tvalid at cycles 13–15. Adding `&& (s_axis_tvalid)` gates the whole frame-drop/overflow block to only real input beats."}, {"id": "patch_44c2dbb83e6a", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 215, "mechanism": "In the FRAME_FIFO=1 design the `!FRAME_FIFO` branch is dead code, but a synthesis-time condition `(!FRAME_FIFO)` that is constant-0 can still be annotated. The candidate rewrites `!FRAME_FIFO` to `(!FRAME_FIFO) && (s_axis_tvalid)`. Though the branch is never taken, the edit forces the write gate to explicitly require s_axis_tvalid in the same syntactic region that produced the spurious m_axis_tvalid at cycles 13–15, reducing the chance that an unqualified combinational path leaks into the FRAME_FIFO logic."}, {"id": "patch_5c0b9ffe4584", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 215, "mechanism": "Similar to patch_44c2dbb83e6a but qualifies with `s_axis_tready` instead of `s_axis_tvalid`. The failure cycles show m_axis_tready=1, so adding `&& (s_axis_tready)` makes the dead branch explicitly dependent on the handshake that is actually asserted when the extra valid appears."}, {"id": "patch_018be7c3f5da", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 215, "mechanism": "Qualifies the dead `!FRAME_FIFO` branch with `full_wr`. During the failing window `full_wr` is low, so the annotated condition stays false and cannot interfere with the live FRAME_FIFO path that is producing the extra m_axis_tvalid."}, {"id": "patch_a4f5abd3f82b", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 215, "mechanism": "Qualifies the dead branch with `!s_axis_tvalid`. In the failing window s_axis_tvalid=1, so `!s_axis_tvalid` is 0 and the annotation keeps the dead branch inactive, avoiding any cross-talk into the FRAME_FIFO write logic that emits the unexpected m_axis_tvalid."}, {"id": "patch_d13bc6261e3c", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 215, "mechanism": "Qualifies the dead branch with `full_wr` (same net effect as patch_018be7c3f5da). During the failure `full_wr`=0, keeping the dead branch disabled."}, {"id": "patch_4dbf02942cc1", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 213, "mechanism": "Changes the write-entry condition from `s_axis_tready && s_axis_tvalid` to `(s_axis_tready && s_axis_tvalid) && (drop_frame_reg)`. In the failure window `drop_frame_reg` is 0, so this would suppress all writes — too strong; ranked low because it over-constrains and would break normal frame acceptance."}, {"id": "patch_33eda120828e", "failure_port": "m_axis_tvalid", "source_line": 213, "mechanism": "Qualifies write-entry with `full_wr`. In the failure `full_wr`=0 so the write gate would close, preventing the frame that eventually causes the extra m_axis_tvalid. Over-constrains like patch_4dbf02942cc1."}], "explanation": "The discovery trace shows three consecutive cycles (13–15) where m_axis_tvalid=1 but the oracle expects 0. The failure window has s_axis_tvalid=1, m_axis_tready=1, and FRAME_FIFO=1. In this configuration the live write logic sits behind the `full_cur || full_wr || drop_frame_reg` gate (line 219). If that gate ever evaluates true on a cycle where s_axis_tvalid is low — for example due to `full_cur` or `full_wr` asserting from pointer state while the bus is idle — the FSM can set `drop_frame_next=1`. On the next real beat the `drop_frame_reg` path forces `wr_ptr_cur` to roll back, making the frame appear accepted and eventually emitting a spurious m_axis_tvalid. The highest-ranked patch (22b3b83e1afe) directly qualifies that gate with `s_axis_tvalid`, ensuring the drop/overflow logic only runs on real input beats. The next patches annotate the dead `!FRAME_FIFO` branch with various handshake signals; they are syntactically nearby and cannot hurt, but they do not touch the live FRAME_FIFO path, so their relevance is lower. Patches that add `drop_frame_reg` or `full_wr` to the write-entry condition (4dbf02942cc1, 33eda120828e) would suppress legitimate writes and are ranked last."}
